doc.what: Myofascial lines ("Anatomy Trains", Myers) as a group family, with the evidence each line has from dissection reviews.
doc.contested: Myofascial lines are a contested concept. Dissection reviews support continuity for some lines (SBL, BFL, FFL), part of others (Spiral, Lateral), none for the Superficial Front Line; the Deep Front Line, the Ipsilateral Functional Line and Myers' four arm lines were not examined by a systematic review. Continuity is not proof of force transmission or of clinical effect. The UI must show the evidence label next to every line.
doc.schema: sub_choices{key: {label, members[] (line ids), ...}}; lines[]: {id, abbr, name, author_family (myers | wilke2019), sub_choices[], composition_refs[], verify_against_book (true: route recorded from the book's standard description without opening the book), crosses_midline, stations[] {station, kind, side (S start side | O opposite | mid | B both), page_bases[], structures {base_m|base_f: {r,l,mid}} or null, on_page, note}, evidence {label strong|moderate|none|not_examined, label_text, wilke2016 {...}, krause2016, refs[]}, note}.
doc.ui: Family "Myofascial lines" -> sub-choice (vertical / diagonal-spiral / functional / arm; horizontal is shown disabled with its "why") -> line list with evidence badges -> selecting a line marks every station's structures. Side: pick the clicked structure's side as S; stations with side O use the other side, mid/B use both lists; when the wanted side list is empty for a body (some midline or one-sided meshes carry an _l/_r suffix) fall back to mid, then to both sides. Bones and fasciae are stations, not the line itself: offer "muscles only" (kind contains "muscle") as the default view.

vertical.label: Vertical (longitudinal) lines
vertical.source: Myers groups the cardinal lines (SBL, SFL, LL) and the DFL as longitudinal; book not opened

diagonal_spiral.label: Diagonal / spiral lines
diagonal_spiral.source: Spiral Line and the two contralateral Functional Lines cross the midline

arm.label: Arm lines
arm.source: Myers (four lines, not examined by a review) + Wilke & Krause 2019 (three chains, reviewed)

horizontal.label: Horizontal bands
horizontal.why: No "horizontal line" exists among Myers' lines or in the reviews opened. The only sourced horizontal concept found is Schultz & Feitis 1996 "body retinacula (bands/straps)" (chest band, inguinal band, ...), seen only as a table of contents; no muscle membership was available. Offer this sub-choice only after the owner decides and a source with members is opened.

kalichman2025.citation: Kalichman L. Myofascial continuity: Review of anatomical and functional evidence. J Bodyw Mov Ther 2025
kalichman2025.opened: abstract via the Consensus search tool (2026-11-15)
kalichman2025.note: Narrative review: strong anatomical support for SBL, BFL, FFL; moderate for Spiral and Lateral lines; SFL lacks validation.

krause2016.citation: Krause F, Wilke J, Vogt L, Banzer W. Intermuscular force transmission along myofascial chains: a systematic review. J Anat 2016;228(6):910-918
krause2016.opened: PubMed abstract (2026-11-15); PMC full text returned empty
krause2016.note: Force transfer (not just continuity): SBL moderate evidence at all 3 transitions (6 studies); BFL 1 of 2 transitions (3 studies); FFL one study, slight non-significant transfer at one transition.

moore2023.citation: Moore JG et al. Anatomization of the upper spiral line: a cadaveric case study of myofascial continuity. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2023 (conference abstract)
moore2023.opened: abstract via the Consensus search tool (2026-11-15)
moore2023.note: One embalmed male cadaver: splenius capitis, splenius cervicis, rhomboid major and minor, serratus anterior, external oblique, internal oblique and rectus abdominis linked by fascia as an upper spiral line.

myers_at.citation: Myers TW. Anatomy Trains: Myofascial Meridians for Manual Therapists and Movement Professionals. Elsevier (1st ed. 2001; 4th ed. 2020)
myers_at.note: NOT opened in this session (copyrighted book; no accessible copy). The station lists below are the line routes as Myers publishes them, recorded from the standard description; every list carries verify_against_book=true until checked against the book.

petrov2026.citation: Petrov OV. Anatomical prerequisites for the existence of myofascial lines: a dissection study. Russian Osteopathic Journal 2026
petrov2026.opened: abstract via the Consensus search tool (2026-11-15)
petrov2026.note: Single cachectic female cadaver: superficial lines reproducible only by adding adjacent fascial/ligamentous components; joints act as switching zones; deep front line could not be separated from visceral structures; concept "only partially confirmed".

schultz1996.citation: Schultz RL, Feitis R. The Endless Web: Fascial Anatomy and Physical Reality. North Atlantic Books, 1996
schultz1996.note: NOT opened. A web search (2026-11-15) showed only its table of contents: Part III "Body retinacula (bands/straps)" with chapters on a chest band and an inguinal band. No muscle lists were seen.

wilke2016.citation: Wilke J, Krause F, Vogt L, Banzer W. What Is Evidence-Based About Myofascial Chains: A Systematic Review. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2016;97(3):454-461

wilke2019.citation: Wilke J, Krause F. Myofascial chains of the upper limb: A systematic review of anatomical studies. Clin Anat 2019;32(7):934-940
